title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is part of Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatic 'Analysis situs' (third version). He works with 'magasins': a set M of 'pieces' carrying three relations.
- ≤ is inclusion.
- ≪ is a strong (relatively compact or interior) inclusion.
- A position relation ≬ (the transcription renders it ≸ or ≭). It reads roughly 'X and Y meet only along their common part', i.e. they are in good relative position.
An alternative presentation uses a separation relation |o| ('strongly disjoint') in place of ≬.

Combinatorial data. Under axioms L1–L3 there is a combinatorial layer L of 'cells' or 'atoms' with a disjointness relation ‖.
- To each X one attaches a set of cells, comb(X). The image may read ouvb(X), and the next page writes ouvb.
- comb(X)° is its 'open' part.
- X̃ is the set of pieces under the closure of X.

Proposition from the previous page. X ≬ Y ⟺ ∀x∈comb(X)°, y∈comb(Y)°, x‖y.

This page.
1. ⇒ is immediate from Mag 5''.
2. To test ⇐, he reverses the viewpoint. Start from a magasin (≤, ≪, ≬) satisfying Mag1–Mag6 (equivalently Prél 1–6, or Mag M1–M6, p. 81) plus L1–L3. Define X |o| Y ⟺ ∀x∈comb(X)°, y∈comb(Y)°, x‖y.
3. He checks that Mag 4'' holds (via At + L3). He checks that Mag 5'' holds by monotonicity: X'≤X ⇒ comb(X')° ⊂ comb(X)°.
4. He then defines ≬' from |o| by the recipe X ≬' Y ⟺ ∀X'∈X̃∖L, Y'∈Ỹ∖L, X'|o|Y', where L = X̃∧Ỹ is the common closed part.
5. Using L2 and the axiom 'At CL', he claims X ≬ Y ⟺ ∀x∈comb(X)∖comb(L), y∈comb(Y)∖comb(L), x‖y.
6. Proof that the right-hand side equals ≬': it rests on the stratification identity comb(X)∖comb(L) = ⋃_{X'∈X̃∖L} comb(X')°, i.e. the closure minus a closed subcomplex is the disjoint union of the open strata not in it, and likewise for Y. The condition on cells then splits stratum by stratum into ∀X',Y' outside L, X'|o|Y', which is exactly X ≬' Y.

Outcome. The ≬-structure and the |o|-structure are mutually recoverable under the L-axioms. The next page's scholium adds that recovering |o| from ≬ alone needs an extra 'divisibility' axiom, Mag 6''.

Purpose. This serves Grothendieck's programme of an axiomatic tame topology ('topologie modérée'): a combinatorial or stratified framework in which relative-position relations among pieces are determined by the face-poset combinatorics of cells.
errors: The ⇐ direction of the proposition is not actually settled on this page. He switches to comparing ≬ with the derived ≬', and the next page concedes that |o| cannot in general be recovered from (≤, ≪, ≬) without Mag 6''.

The decomposition comb(X)∖comb(L) = ⋃ comb(X')° is used without proof. It presupposes that the strata in X̃ partition the cells of the closure and that L is a down-closed (closed) subset; this is presumably what L1–L3 guarantee.
The transcription's 'comb' may be a misreading of 'ouvb', which is the spelling used on the next page. The mathematics is unaffected.

ideas.what: Axiomatic 'magasin' with inclusion, strong inclusion, and a relative-position (disjointness) relation, modelling tame/stratified spaces
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic tame topology; o-minimal structures / stratified sets (abstract mereotopology-like axiomatics)
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1980s); the tame-topology programme is credited to Grothendieck's Esquisse (1984)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 announces tame topology; the magasin axioms themselves appear only in these unpublished notes

ideas.what: The closure of a stratum minus a closed substratification is the union of the open strata outside it; disjointness conditions decompose cellwise
ideas.modern_name: Face-poset / stratification decomposition (regular cell complexes, Whitney/Thom stratifications)

ideas.what: Equivalence of two presentations of the separation structure (≬ versus |o|), via the cellwise condition x‖y on L
ideas.modern_name: Recovering relations on a poset of strata from relations on its cells (a Galois-type correspondence)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches an axiomatic, purely order-theoretic tame topology. In it, relative-position relations between pieces are determined by a combinatorial cell layer L. The two presentations (≬ versus |o|) are equivalent only under an extra divisibility axiom (Mag 6''). This axiom system was never developed or published.
missed.quote: Si on part d'une magnifique structure (≤, ≪, ≭), décrite par Mag 1 – Mag 6 ... et si on suppose aussi L1, L2, L3, alors on pourrait définir raisonnablement X |o| Y ⟺ ∀x∈comb(X)°, y∈comb(Y)°, on a x‖y
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: An axiomatic, point-free approach to tame topology could be compared with o-minimal combinatorics, mereotopology and locale-theoretic approaches. Specialists may not know Grothendieck attempted such axioms in 1986. On this page, however, the content is routine bookkeeping.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a technical verification inside an unpublished axiomatic tame-topology framework. Its mathematical content (a cellwise decomposition of a disjointness condition) is routine. Only the existence of the framework itself is of mild historical interest.
transcription_corrections: 'comb(X)°' is probably 'ouvb(X)°', consistent with the next page's 'ouvb'.
The relation written ≸ or ≭ is likely the same symbol as the next page's ≬ ('between'-style).
'magnifique structure' is likely 'magasin structure' or 'magasinique structure', referring to the 'magasin' axioms.
Line 2 of the page: 'Il faut voir si on a ⟸' is fine.
